- When sentiment history shows a recent spike (e.g., 1.00) followed by a flat or declining trend, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% in subsequent periods.
- Model consistently overestimates price in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- After a strong upward spike in true outcome, model often fails to fully correct — apply mean reversion adjustment: subtract 1–3% from forecast 3–5 days after peak.
- If sentiment history is flat (all 0.00) for 10+ days, model tends to underpredict — increase forecast by 1–2% for first 3–5 days of horizon.
- Model exhibits lag in capturing sentiment-driven reversals — if sentiment turns negative or neutral after a spike, delay forecast correction by 1–2 days and reduce slope of decline.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overweights recent history — reduce weight of last 3–5 days in smoothing when sentiment is stable or negative.
